au.csiro.JamesGunning.seismicinverter
Class MCMCConvergenceMonitor

java.lang.Object
  |
  +--au.csiro.JamesGunning.seismicinverter.MCMCConvergenceMonitor
public final class MCMCConvergenceMonitor
extends java.lang.Object

A class designed to monitor convergence in two possible ways.

(1) as per suggestions on p 331 of Gelman et al "Bayesian Statistics". Read these pages to make sense of this Class. The discussion is very similar to Ch. 8 of "Markov Chain Monte Carlo in Practice", Gilks et al; entitled "Inference and monitoring convergence". For the time being, we use internal layer times as the scalar estimands. These seem to be most susceptible to non-stationarity, or slow convergence.

(2) There are also some utility routines for comuting the most optimal decimation of a single sequence, which we call Raftery-style decimation, as per Raftery et al, Ch 7, "Markov Chain Monte Carlo in Practice", Gilks et al. See also Raftery, A.E. and Lewis, S.M. (1992) "How many iterations in the Gibbs sampler?" In Bayesian Statistics, Vol. 4 (J.M. Bernardo, J.O. Berger, A.P. Dawid and A.F.M. Smith, eds.). Oxford, U.K.: Oxford University Press, 763-773. This paper is available via the World Wide Web by linking to URL http://www.stat.washington.edu/tech.reports/pub/tech.reports and then selecting the "How Many Iterations in the Gibbs Sampler" link. A useful reference is also Bishop, Feinberg & Holland, "Discrete Multivariate Analysis" MIT Press.
Here we have freely translated a few salient routines from the gibbsit code - mainly the calls required to compute the thinning constant.

Compute some convergence diagnostics as per suggestions on p 331 of Gelman et al "Bayesian Statistics". Read these pages to make sense of this Class. The discussion is very similar to Ch. 8 of "Markov Chain Monte Carlo in Practice", Gilks et al; entitled "Inference and monitoring convergence". We use i,j, in Gelman's sense, and k to run over the scalar estimands of choice. For the time being, we use internal layer times as the scalar estimands. These seem to be most susceptible to non-stationarity, or slow convergence. Here we initilise things.

completeScalarEstimandsUpdate

void completeScalarEstimandsUpdate(int sample_number)
Here we complete operations on the psi scalar estimands. The scalar_estimands[] array is expected to be filled with the desired values by this stage.

If doing Gelman monitoring, as per Gelman p 331, the indices i (current position in the chain) and j (current member of ensemble (j=1...N_INDEPENDENT_CHAINS, (we use ensemble_cntr)) are taken as implicit.

If doing Raftery-style, the desired scalars are stored for later use

Parameters:
sample_number - is the sample in the current sequence, must be 0....(_m._SI.n_samples_per_trace_undecimated-1)

getRafteryWorstCaseThinningRecommendation

int getRafteryWorstCaseThinningRecommendation()
After a successful call to performConvergenceDiagnosticsWhileSamplingFromLocalModes(), if RafteryStyleDiagnostics==true (we are doing Raftery style), this method reveals the recommended thinning parameter for the Markov chain. No recommendation greater than MAXIMUM_RAFTERY_DECIMATION_FACTOR will be returned.

initialiseRafteryStyleConvergenceDiagnostics

                                                  int n_samples_in_chain)
Compute some convergence diagnostics as per Raftery-style suggestions in "Markov Chain Monte Carlo in Practice", Gilks et al; Chapter 7. See also Raftery, A.E. and Lewis, S.M. (1992). How many iterations in the Gibbs sampler? In Bayesian Statistics, Vol. 4 (J.M. Bernardo, J.O. Berger, A.P. Dawid and A.F.M. Smith, eds.). We use internal layer times as the scalar estimands - these are thresholded at suitable values to produce the 0,1 sequences required. These seem to be most susceptible to non-stationarity, or slow convergence
